comment: Findings accepted as decisions rather than defects. Each key is 'axis::symbol'; the value is why it is accepted. Delete an entry to make the audit report it again. Add entries with --update-known, but write a real reason afterwards — an unexplained entry is indistinguishable from a bug someone silenced.

accepted.nonfinite::lucid.sign: sign(NaN) returns 0 rather than NaN. Consistent across cpu and metal, and the GPU path inherits MLX's own sign convention, so this is a convention Lucid has taken rather than an internal disagreement. Changing it would mean patching NaN on every GPU sign call and altering three internal consumers (L1 norm backward, abs backward, the relu mask). Reviewed 2026-08-02.
accepted.nonfinite::Tensor.sign: Same decision as nonfinite::lucid.sign — one op, two spellings.
accepted.entry::lucid.repeat: ``lucid.repeat`` and ``Tensor.repeat`` are deliberately different operations. The free function is NumPy's ``repeat`` — element-wise, so (2,2) with repeats=2 along dim 1 gives (2,4) — and the method is the reference framework's ``Tensor.repeat``, which tiles, giving (4,2). ``lucid/_ops/_registry.py`` states the choice explicitly at both entries. Each meaning is also available under an unambiguous name: ``repeat_interleave`` and ``tile``. Not silenced because it is harmless — sharing a name across two semantics is a real trap — but because changing it is an API decision rather than a defect fix. Reviewed 2026-08-03.
accepted.entry::Tensor.repeat: Same decision as entry::lucid.repeat — the two spellings are the point.
accepted.entry::lucid.einops.repeat: Same decision as entry::lucid.repeat; einops' repeat is a third convention again, named by its own package.
accepted.device::F.scaled_dot_product_attention: A query that is entirely NaN gives 0 on the CPU and NaN on Metal. The CPU's answer matches the reference framework's exactly, and neither is computed: a flash-attention accumulator starts its running maximum at -inf and its output at 0, and no NaN score ever beats the maximum, so nothing accumulates and the initialisation is what comes back. MLX's kernel propagates instead. Verified that this is the *only* case that differs — a NaN in one key row or one value row gives NaN on both devices and in the reference — so no NaN is being swallowed in any input a network would produce. Making Metal agree would mean writing code whose only purpose is to reproduce an accumulator artefact, and making the CPU agree with Metal would break parity with the reference. Reviewed 2026-08-04.
accepted.nonfinite::F.scaled_dot_product_attentio: Same decision as device::F.scaled_dot_product_attention — one behaviour, two axes looking at it.
accepted.module::nn.VectorQuantizer: The axis backpropagates from the forward output and requires some parameter to receive a gradient. For this module that is false by construction, and the falseness is the entire point: quantisation is a hard argmin, so the straight-through estimator routes the decoder's gradient *past* the codebook onto the layer's input. The codebook is trained by the separately-returned ``codebook_loss`` (||sg[x] - e||^2), which the module also hands back — so the layer does train, just not through the tensor the axis measures. Not fixed in the axis: teaching it to backprop from whichever output happens to produce a gradient would let a module whose primary output is accidentally detached pass on the strength of an incidental auxiliary tensor, which is the defect this axis exists to catch. ``lucid/test/unit/nn/modules/test_vector_quantizer.py`` asserts the routing in both directions instead — reconstruction reaches the input and not the codebook, the codebook term reaches the codebook and not the input. See [[arch-vector-quantization-layering]]. Reviewed 2026-08-14.
